items.title: Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2013
items.q: And Gershwin heard William Grant Still improvise it.

ctx.x: Oh it’s been a lifelong process. And that’s actually somewhat of a separate question, but then what I would describe that this has been an idea that germinated since my childhood. During the 1960’s I spent my childhood in Palo Alto, and that’s located, that’s where Stanford University is located. And I was often reminded that Stanford built the railroad. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -1-

So in 1963 the Chinese Historical Society of America was founded, and my uncle Philip Choy was one of the longtime leaders. He wasn’t a founder, but he was a longtime leader. And in 1969, which was supposed to be the celebration of the centennial anniversary of the completion of the transcontinental railroad, which was held in Utah and was celebrated by the U.S. government, there was a keynote speaker named John Volpe, he was the secretary of transportation. And he kept repeating, “it was American workers that…
Yeah. It was like Ellington listening to his guys warm up, and using pieces of their warm- up when writing a tune. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -2-
